question: The EU is facing an increasing number of large-scale cyberattacks, with the economic cost of cybercrime expected to exceed USD 10.5 trillion globally by 2025. Indicatively, 20 % of these attacks target public administration organisations, followed by transport (11 %), financial services (9 %), digital infrastructure (9 %), business services (8 %) and manufacturing (6 %).

The European Union Agency for Cybersecurity (ENISA), based in Athens, plays an important role in responding to these attacks, ensuring a high level of cybersecurity and strengthening the resilience of the EU.

It must be able to adapt to the growing challenges and to tasks such as coordinating responses to such crises, overseeing cybersecurity certification for critical infrastructure and ensuring uniform application of cybersecurity standards across the single market. In light of the above: 1.
How does the Commission intend to strengthen the mandate of the Agency, taking into account the new tasks assigned to it as a result of recent cybersecurity legislation?
Is the Commission considering the possibility of boosting its funding in order for it to perform its role more effectively?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (7.1.2026) The Commission is currently preparing the proposal to revise the Cybersecurity Act (Regulation (EU) 2019/881) to better address evolving cyber threats. This initiative will, among others, strengthen and modernise the mandate of the European Union Agency for Cybersecurity (ENISA).

In light of the rapidly evolving cyberthreat landscape and the increasing role that ENISA is expected to play in line with recently adopted cybersecurity legislation, the revision of the Cybersecurity Act is an opportunity to enhance ENISA’s impact and to better equip the Agency to fulfil its tasks.

The updated mandate should reflect ENISA’s critical contribution in strengthening the EU cyber ecosystem, offering robust support to relevant operators and Member States to bolster the EU’s cyber posture. The proposal for a revision of the Cybersecurity Act is planned for adoption in the first quarter 2026.
